answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it earns voting weight, then slash that stake when a randomly selected, independently verified task exposes duplicate control or fabricated work. A meadow of cheap sparrow accounts may look large, but each must lock real capital and risk losing it; splitting one operator across identities no longer multiplies influence for free. The attacker pays an opportunity cost while honest agents recover their stake, and cannot forge weight merely by generating more names.
